readings.title: The invitation nobody answered
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A community centre sent new residents a translated invitation to an open meeting. Few replied. Staff first wondered whether the translation was inaccurate. A volunteer pointed out that the message asked readers to 'confirm attendance' without explaining how or whether a reply was required to enter. The next invitation gave a phone number, a deadline and a statement that drop-in visitors were welcome. Replies increased, and more people attended without booking. Translation had carried the words into another language, but practical clarity required examining what readers needed to do. The revised message helped long-term residents as well as newcomers.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：细节、推断、词义与主旨

readings.title: A word list built together
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: An adult class studying workplace English received a long list of technical words. Learners memorised definitions but struggled to use them in conversations. Their tutor asked each person to bring one real situation in which a term was needed. A cleaner described reporting a loose cable; a driver explained a delivery delay. The class built short exchanges around these examples and added common alternatives. The list became shorter but more closely connected to use. Learners still needed precise terms, yet understanding included knowing when a word was useful, whom to say it to and what response might follow.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：细节、推断、词义与主旨

readings.title: The pause in the meeting
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: During a joint project, Arun noticed that one colleague rarely spoke immediately after a question. He assumed she had little to contribute and often filled the silence himself. Later, she sent detailed written observations that changed the team's plan. Arun realised that his quick response habit left little room for people who preferred time to organise thoughts in a second language. At the next meeting, he circulated questions in advance and allowed a short thinking pause. More members contributed. The adjustment did not lower expectations; it changed the conditions under which different people could meet them.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：细节、推断、词义与主旨

readings.title: The name on the badge
readings.instruction: Read the original passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: At a training event, organisers printed participants' names from a registration form. Several badges shortened unfamiliar names without asking. One participant explained that the shortened form was not a name she used. The organiser apologised and offered blank badges so everyone could choose how to be addressed. She also added a preferred-name field to future forms. The change was small, but it affected the opening conversation: participants no longer had to begin by correcting an unwanted label. Accuracy in a name was not merely an administrative detail; it was part of making space for a person to introduce themselves.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：细节、推断、词义与主旨

translation.stem:
Translate this original passage into Chinese.

Understanding another person is not always a matter of finding an equivalent word. People bring different expectations about politeness, silence and agreement to a conversation. Asking a respectful question can reveal these differences before they become a source of conflict. Effective communication grows when participants are willing to examine their own assumptions as well as explain their intentions.
translation.referenceAnswer: 理解另一个人并不总是找到对应词语那么简单。人们对礼貌、沉默和同意抱有不同的期待，并把这些期待带入交谈。在差异成为冲突来源之前，尊重地提问能使其显现。参与者既愿意解释自身意图，也愿意审视自己的假设时，有效沟通才能发展。
translation.explanation: 参考译文展示一种可接受的表达；保留原文信息及逻辑、中文通顺的其他译法同样有效。

writing.stem:
Write about 120 English words for this original simulation task.

Write advice for a project group whose members have different first languages. Include ways to prepare for meetings, support participation and confirm decisions.
writing.sampleAnswer: Before a meeting, our group should share a short agenda and explain unfamiliar terms with examples. Members can then prepare ideas without the pressure of understanding everything immediately. During discussion, speakers should use clear sentences and allow others time to respond. A pause does not necessarily mean that someone has nothing to contribute. The chair can invite comments without forcing anyone to speak before they are ready. Important points should be restated when needed, and questions should be welcomed. After the meeting, one member should circulate a brief record of decisions, responsibilities and deadlines. Everyone can confirm or correct that record. These habits help the group work accurately while respecting different ways of expressing ideas.
writing.explanation: 范文用于作答后参考；观点与例子可以不同，但须回应全部要求并表达清楚。
